messages:
marta (People Ops): quick Q from a manager — new external hire is slated to start the same week an internal promo is targeted. manager asked: what are evidence cutoffs, retro timing, and how do equity grants line up if headcount merges?

josh (Eng Manager): ah great, classic timing issue. if we make the candidate an internal transfer on day 1, does payroll treat it as a hire or a comp change?

marta (People Ops): short answer: it depends. internal transfer/role-change where the person already exists in payroll = comp change. fresh external hire = new hire flow. both require manager sign-off and evidence to hit an effective date.

sana (Recruiter): candidate verbally accepted 2026-04-08, proposed start 2026-05-04. manager wants promo effective 2026-05-01. is that feasible to align?

ethan (Payroll): payroll cutoffs you need to know: monthly processing has a 10th cutoff for changes to be included in the first following monthly payroll run; we also have a 24th mid-month batch. if paperwork arrives after the cutoff we must process the change retroactively in the next cycle. for urgent compliance fixes we can do manual adjustments but that's exception-only. pinging @payroll-bot to validate intake flow.

marta (People Ops): concrete for these dates: to get the 2026-05-01 effective date into May payroll, submit the comp_change_form + evidence by 2026-05-10 (23:59 PT). missing that means the pay runs at existing comp and payroll will issue retro in the next cycle (expect one payroll delay).

ethan (Payroll): required items: manager sign-off (email OK), evidence bundle (role description + comp rationale), completed comp_change_form, and grant request if equity is needed. use intake: https://hiring.redwood.com/evidence-upload or internal form. payroll-bot will ack and do a format check. sample CSV we accept: 

```
employee_id,full_name,effective_date,new_base,grant_needed,manager
12345,Alex Rivera,2026-05-01,160000,yes,Josh Lee
```

marta (People Ops): equity note: grant creation happens after comp change approval. grant creation follows the grant calendar and usually appears in the equity system in 2-3 business days. vesting schedules don't change; just the record creation timing may lag. attach grant rationale to evidence so we can queue it immediately.

alex (Hiring Manager): if we hire externally but then convert to internal transfer right away, do we need a separate grant from the promo flow or does the offer cover it?

marta (People Ops): either approach is fine but must be explicit: if the offer includes equity, that grant is created from the offer. if you onboard as an external hire and then process an internal comp_change + grant, the grant is a separate request. always attach rationale and approve via manager.

josh (Eng Manager): let's make a short checklist for the team so nothing slips: 1) manager sign-off email, 2) evidence (role scope + comp rationale), 3) completed comp_change_form, 4) mark grant_needed on the form + attach rationale, 5) submit by payroll cutoff.

sana (Recruiter): i'll sync timelines with the candidate and push for completed forms before 2026-05-10. if we risk missing the cutoff i'll ask for an exception.

ethan (Payroll): exceptions: open a payroll emergency ticket with justification and org approval. manual adjustments are possible but not guaranteed and add operational risk. include employee id, requested effective date, and approver name.

marta (People Ops): i'll turn this into a tiny how-to note in #people-ops resources so hiring managers can follow the checklist. react with :thumbsup: when you have what you need or :warning: if you want me to escalate.
